reviewType: Targeted appraisal of named primary studies and official guidelines; not an exhaustive systematic review or formal GRADE assessment

gradeDefinitions.A: Strong support for a narrowly specified endpoint in the appraised evidence; not a blanket clinical recommendation
gradeDefinitions.B: Moderate or mixed evidence with material limits on certainty or applicability
gradeDefinitions.C: Emerging or limited evidence, including small, observational, indirect or access-limited studies

limitations: Grades summarize this bounded source set; they are project editorial judgements, not validated clinical recommendations. Preserve review scope and limitations alongside each badge.
Evidence direction, evidence quality and regulatory approval are separate fields.
No dosing instructions are derived. Current guidance and additional studies can change an appraisal.
Publication-count queries through 2025 and current evidence appraisal through the review date serve different purposes.

data.question: Patient-reported acne improvement in adult women, alongside permitted topical treatment
data.design: Pragmatic blinded placebo-controlled RCT plus official guideline summary
data.biasAndPrecision: Independent randomization and masking reported; modified intention-to-treat analysis with missing-data sensitivity analysis. Primary improvement was modest and its clinically important threshold uncertain.
data.applicability: Adult women; later follow-up showed larger differences. Do not generalize to every age, sex or acne presentation.
data.interpretation: Supported option in the studied population, with conditional guideline context; project grade B reflects remaining certainty and applicability limits.

data.question: Hirsutism management in PCOS, rather than treatment of all PCOS manifestations
data.biasAndPrecision: The relevant PCOS antiandrogen recommendation has very-low-certainty evidence; recommendation strength is not equivalent to strong trial evidence.
data.applicability: Hirsutism-specific context, with pregnancy-prevention restrictions and previous-treatment qualifications retained in the source.
data.interpretation: A guideline-supported conditional role with limited underlying evidence; no blanket PCOS efficacy or approval claim.

data.question: Additional benefit for female pattern hair loss when added to topical minoxidil
data.biasAndPrecision: Randomization and allocation concealment reported; 48 randomized with attrition. Primary hair-count comparison did not meet the conventional significance threshold, while photographic secondary outcomes favored treatment.
data.applicability: Premenopausal women and combination treatment; not evidence for spironolactone monotherapy or all alopecia.
data.interpretation: Promising but imprecise, endpoint-dependent evidence; the PRD's observational-only seed is outdated.

data.question: TOPCAT primary composite outcome in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
data.design: Large blinded randomized placebo-controlled trial; abstract-level appraisal here
data.biasAndPrecision: The primary confidence interval crossed the null. Secondary hospitalization findings must not replace the primary outcome; full-text bias, regional and subgroup appraisal remains incomplete.
data.applicability: Specific trial EF/population definition; cannot borrow the reduced-EF label or generalize subgroup findings to all HFpEF.
data.interpretation: No significant reduction in the overall primary composite; retain secondary signals as qualified context rather than a positive headline.

data.question: Short-term home blood-pressure reduction as add-on therapy in resistant hypertension
data.design: Blinded randomized crossover comparison against placebo and two active drugs
data.biasAndPrecision: Randomization/masking reported and hierarchy of blood-pressure comparisons specified. Participants without follow-up were excluded and missing-at-random assumptions apply.
data.applicability: Short exposure, selected kidney-function eligibility and predominantly white participants limit extrapolation. Cardiovascular outcome benefit was not the measured endpoint.
data.interpretation: Strong evidence for the specified BP endpoint, not long-term outcome superiority. This use is not automatically off-label under the US add-on hypertension indication.

data.question: Breast development with spironolactone versus cyproterone alongside estradiol
data.design: Small blinded active-comparator randomized trial plus official guideline summary
data.biasAndPrecision: Independent randomized allocation and masking reported; short follow-up, limited sample and measurement limitations reduce certainty. A nonsignificant difference is not proof of equivalence.
data.applicability: Comparative treatment with concomitant estradiol; cannot establish the independent absolute contribution of spironolactone to all feminising outcomes.
data.interpretation: Direct comparative evidence now exists, but endpoints and regimen context must remain explicit; project grade B is scoped to that comparison.

data.question: Anatomical fluid reduction versus visual benefit in persistent central serous chorioretinopathy
data.biasAndPrecision: Very small sample, short treatment periods and carryover concerns. Anatomical fluid measures improved while visual-acuity differences were not significant.
data.applicability: Persistent disease in the selected study eyes; no established broad visual benefit from this source set.
data.interpretation: Emerging anatomical signal, not sufficient evidence for an unqualified clinical-benefit claim.

data.question: Treatment response in women with hidradenitis suppurativa
data.biasAndPrecision: No randomized untreated comparator; confounding by severity, co-treatment, selection and response assessment are material. Association is not a causal treatment effect.
data.applicability: Selected clinical cohort; severe disease and response definitions affect findings.
data.interpretation: Limited observational evidence; do not use response percentages as generalized efficacy estimates.

data.question: PMS symptoms in the historical trial population, not a PMDD efficacy claim
data.design: Small placebo-controlled crossover study; abstract-only appraisal
data.biasAndPrecision: Small sample and reported carryover; full allocation, attrition and analysis methods were not available for appraisal.
data.applicability: Historical PMS diagnosis and symptom measures cannot be assumed to establish efficacy for modern PMDD criteria.
data.interpretation: Limited PMS signal; keep PMDD ungraded and avoid extending this badge to a PMDD treatment claim.

data.question: Proteinuria reduction in CKD; separate from cardiovascular protection
data.design: Open-label randomized proteinuria study (abstract) plus a larger cardiovascular-outcome trial (full text)
data.biasAndPrecision: Proteinuria is a surrogate and the earlier study was open-label. BARACK-D did not demonstrate cardiovascular benefit in its population and had substantial treatment discontinuation; it recruited below its original target.
data.applicability: Different populations and endpoints cannot be pooled into one CKD-benefit conclusion; evidence for other mineralocorticoid antagonists is not interchangeable.
data.interpretation: Limited evidence for the proteinuria question; preserve the separate negative cardiovascular result as context. No blanket CKD benefit or prescribing recommendation.
